10.1002_adfm.202519538: Aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries (ZIBs) have attracted tremendous attention due to their high energy density and good safety. However, their applications are hindered by the lack of desirable I 2 hosts that can suppress polyiodide shuttle and improve I 2 /I − conversion simultaneously. Herein, a cathode host (P‐HCS) composed of hollow carbon spheres (HCS) and poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) nanowires is reported. The charge transfer from PEDOT to I 2 molecules induces partial conversion of I 2 to I 3 − which are confined between the π‐stacked interchains. Such strong interactions between PEDOT nanowire and I 3 − contribute to capturing polyiodides and suppressing their shuttles. Meanwhile, theoretical calculations reveal that PEDOT nanowires can promote I 2 /I − conversion reactions by lowering Gibbs free energy. Consequently, a ZIB with I 2 ‐P‐HCS cathode delivers a reversible capacity of 214 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , while retaining 91% capacity and 99.8% coulombic efficiency over 47 000 cycles at 10 A g −1 . A high specific capacity and satisfying stability are also achieved at a high I 2 mass loading of 7.1 mg cm −2 , making PEDOT nanowires an ideal polymer that can realize fast I 2 /I − conversion reactions and shuttle suppression simultaneously.
10.1002_smll.202514722: Single‐atom Fe sites coordinated by pyrrolic nitrogen (Fe‐N pyrr ‐C) are highly active for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) but suffer from rapid demetalization‐induced deactivation. Here, we overcome this limitation via a Mg‐assisted sacrificial templating strategy that precisely reconstructs Fe‐N 4 coordination, driving partial conversion of unstable pyrrolic‐N to robust pyridinic‐N ligands. The resulting Fe(Mg)‐N‐C(1) catalyst exhibits exceptional ORR performance (half‐wave potential E 1/2 = 0.91 V) and outstanding durability, retaining 95.2% of its initial current after 55 h, surpassing both Fe‐N‐C and Pt/C. In Zn‐air batteries, it enables stable operation for > 530 h (peak power density: 271 mW cm − 2 ). This work demonstrates that enriching pyridinic‐N‐coordinated Fe‐N 4 sites simultaneously enhances activity and suppresses demetalization, offering a general coordination‐engineering strategy to unify activity and stability in Fe‐N‐C electrocatalysts.
10.1016_j.applthermaleng.2026.131692: Water scarcity is intensifying worldwide, driving the need for desalination technologies that are compact, energy-efficient, and suitable for decentralized operation. This study investigates a multistage direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) system powered solely by distributed solar energy to enhance freshwater productivity while maintaining compactness. The work extends a previously demonstrated single-stage concept to multistage operation under ambient-temperature feed conditions, without external feed preheating, active cooling, or solar concentration. Two configurations are examined: (i) a counter-current multistage system with external heat exchange for cooling, used as a benchmark, and (ii) a fully self-contained configuration relying exclusively on internal thermal management. A numerical model is developed and validated against experimental data, showing good agreement. An optimization algorithm is then employed to determine optimal feed and permeate mass flow rates and to assess the effects of stage number and solar irradiance. Results show that the externally cooled configuration exhibits an approximately linear increase in specific productivity with the number of stages, reaching 1.71 kg m$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$ for four-stage configuration under 700 W m$^{-2}$. The configuration with internal heat recovery further enhances performance, achieving 2.33 kg m$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$ and a gain output ratio of 1.58. Model extrapolation indicates potential productivity up to about 3 and 4 kg m$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$ for seven-stage configuration at 700 and 1000 W m$^{-2}$, respectively, with emerging saturation effects. Compared with state-of-the-art compact MD systems powered by distributed solar energy, the proposed design enables higher absolute freshwater production under ambient feed conditions, demonstrating a scalable and energy-efficient solution for off-grid desalination.
10.1109_tte.2026.3690512: As the safety demands of electrified transportation escalate, solid-state batteries (SSBs) are emerging to replace traditional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet their thermal runaway (TR) mechanisms remain poorly understood. Current research on TR warning focuses on LIBs and relies on contact-based electrical methods, most notably electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Theoretically, the fixed perturbation signal’s repeated calculation within EIS causes information redundancy since only the response varies. Practically, the methods fail at high temperatures due to interfacial impedance heterogeneity in SSBs. To overcome these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel dual-stage TR warning framework fusing contact-based electrical and non-contact magnetic sensing. Stage 1 implements online hardware assessing SSBs’ response to a 1 kHz perturbation, extracting novel time-frequency indicators to eliminate computational redundancy, achieving a 9-minute earlier TR warning than conventional assessment. Stage 2 deploys magnetic monitoring for explosion precursors, providing 20-second advance warning.
